review_comment:
Just to verify my understanding of why we need this setting. Is it for cases where the mapping does contain a `host.name` field but the user doesn't want it to be used for sorting purposes? I suppose that is to have parity with the previous behavior where you could disable sorting by `host.name` by manually specifying just `@timestamp` as a sort field. Did I get that right?

Nit: there's a discrepancy in the naming (`SORT_ON_HOST_NAME` vs `use_default_sort_config`). The latter seems a bit more generic in case we add more fields to the default sort config. But either way, I think it makes sense to keep the name of the config option and the constant aligned.

The idea here is that, if we detect that the mappings contain a field (not object) `host.name`, it's used for sorting. Otherwise, we only sort on `@timestamp`. The rationale is that there's no point to inject `host.name` and sort on it if the mappings don't indicate that it's already present and used.

Good catch about the discrepancy - initially I had 2 settings to separately control injecting `host.name` and sorting on it. It feels cleaner to skip injection, but I'm really interested on your take here.

As mentioned in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/118968#discussion_r1899523137, I think it's important to still support dynamically mapped `host.name` fields. This could either be achieved by injecting `host.name` or by introducing this sorting hash we talked about.
Wouldn't `host.name` get injected from a dynamic template in this case? What if `host` gets dynamically mapped to a keyword as well, without `subobjects:false`?

> Wouldn't host.name get injected from a dynamic template in this case?

Not entirely sure what you mean. But there doesn't need to be a dynamic template that's specific to `host.name`, it could just be one that maps strings to keywords by default.

> What if host gets dynamically mapped to a keyword as well, without subobjects:false?

That would be an issue indeed. Still better than the current default that always injects the host.name. I suppose we'll eventually need a solution that doesn't depend on injecting a mapping but also fully supports dynamic mappings. The only solution that comes to my mind that reconciles the two is the sorting hash approach.
ok I've restored the second setting for injecting `host.name` when possible.
